title: Windrow House Rising Revisited
premise: When the coffin of town founder Augustus Windrow is found empty during a cathedral restoration, archivist Quentin Vasquez realizes the 'accidental' deaths of three people connected to a thirty-year-old land deal were anything but. Following a trail of forged burial records, hidden deeds, and a witness who faked his own death, Quentin uncovers a conspiracy protected by the town's most respected families—and by her own late mentor, whose alibi for the night of the original crime unravels everything she believed about him. As the conspirators close in, Quentin must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the fragile found family she has built among the cathedral staff. In the end, she stages a public reckoning inside Windrow House itself, forcing a confession before the whole town, and finds that belonging was never something she had to earn—it was something she had to claim.
about_author: M. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloging centuries of births, deaths, and quiet scandals in small-town New England archives. Their mysteries are known for meticulous historical detail and protagonists who find family in unlikely places.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Quentin Vasquez catalogs the cathedral crypt's oldest ledgers, establishing her solitary routine and her unspoken history of solving three deaths the police dismissed. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Ground Broken
chapters.summary: Restoration crews begin exhuming founder Augustus Windrow for reinterment; Quentin notices the sexton's hands shaking as he signs the permit. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: unease beneath civic celebration.

chapters.title: An Empty Box
chapters.summary: The coffin is opened before the town council: it holds only river stones and a rotted prayer book. The mayor calls it vandalism; Quentin recognizes the stones are from the millrace where a man drowned in 1994. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: cold shock.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Quentin cross-references burial records and finds Augustus's interment entry written in ink manufactured after his supposed death year. Someone falsified the archive—her archive. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: violated trust in her own sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Drowning Man
chapters.summary: Flashback-adjacent research chapter: Quentin reconstructs the 1994 death of millworker Tomás Reyes, ruled accidental, whose case shares signatures with the three deaths she previously solved. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: dawning pattern recognition.

chapters.title: Tea with the Widow
chapters.summary: Quentin visits elderly Marisol Reyes, Tomás's widow, who reveals Tomás claimed he'd found documents proving the Windrow land grant was fraudulent days before he drowned. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief handed across generations.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Quentin maps the deaths of the notary, the surveyor, and the priest who all touched the land documents between 1994 and now—each within weeks of an anniversary. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into certainty.

chapters.title: Father Anselm's Warning
chapters.summary: The cathedral's aging pastor gently urges Quentin to leave it alone, revealing he knows more than he says; she catches him burning a letter. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: betrayal by a father figure.

chapters.title: The Kitchen Table Society
chapters.summary: Quentin finally confides in her found family—organist Dee, groundskeeper Bo, and teenage volunteer Sam—who insist on helping despite the danger. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: warmth against isolation.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Quentin discovers every suspect has an airtight alibi for the night Tomás died—all anchored to the same charity gala, guest lists preserved in the very archive she keeps. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the past watching her back.

chapters.title: Windrow House
chapters.summary: A tour of the founder's preserved mansion introduces the current heir, Cordelia Windrow-Hale, charming and watchful, who offers Quentin access to family papers. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: seduction of the gilded cage.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Bo discovers a second empty plot in the pauper's section—Tomás Reyes's grave is also vacant, disturbed long ago. Two empty coffins, one conspiracy. POV: Bo. Emotional beat: fear made physical.

chapters.title: Ink and Water
chapters.summary: Sam helps Quentin test the forged ledger page; the water damage pattern proves the record was rewritten after the 2019 flood, narrowing suspects to those with post-flood archive access. POV: Sam. Emotional beat: the kid proving essential.

chapters.title: Dee's Hymn
chapters.summary: Dee recalls playing the gala in 1994 and remembers one guest leaving early, soaked to the knees—someone whose presence in the official record Quentin cannot find at all. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: memory as testimony.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Quentin identifies the unrecorded guest: Elias Crane, the estate lawyer who vanished in 1995, presumed drowned—yet his signature appears on a deed dated two years later. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the dead walking through paperwork.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Quentin returns to find her research notes reordered and a pressed lily—Augustus Windrow's funeral flower—left on her desk. A message: we know. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: hunted in her own home ground.

chapters.title: Police, Politely
chapters.summary: Detective Ibarra, whom Quentin once helped quietly, warns her off officially while slipping her an old evidence photo: Tomás's boots, mud from somewhere upstream of the millrace. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: alliance across institutional lines.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Quentin and Bo trace the mud to a sealed well on the old Windrow orchard, where they find a rusted strongbox containing the original land grant—with a second signature line torn away. POV: Bo. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into target on their backs.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Kindness
chapters.summary: Cordelia hosts Quentin at Windrow House, offering protection and partnership; Quentin notices the torn edge of a document framed above the fireplace matches her strongbox paper. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: charm as camouflage.

chapters.title: The Mentor's File
chapters.summary: In her late mentor's locked drawer, Quentin finds his private investigation into the land fraud—abruptly abandoned in 1995, with a note: 'E.C. is alive. Do not pursue.' Her mentor knew. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: What Father Anselm Buried
chapters.summary: Confronted, Anselm confesses he helped hide Elias Crane in the monastery years ago under a vow of silence, believing it penance, not complicity. He gives Quentin the monastery's visitor log. POV: Anselm. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution too late.

chapters.title: Crane in the Flesh
chapters.summary: Following the log, Quentin finds Elias Crane alive, old and dying, living as a lay brother. He admits he faked his death to escape the conspirators—but swears he didn't kill Tomás. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: pity complicating pursuit.

chapters.title: The Confession That Isn't
chapters.summary: Crane claims Tomás died accidentally during a panicked confrontation and that someone else moved both bodies' coffins recently—to destroy evidence someone was digging. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: truth wearing a mask of confession.

chapters.title: Sam Follows the Flower
chapters.summary: Sam stakes out a florist supplying lilies and photographs the buyer: the cathedral's own business manager, Ruth Okafor, who has quietly controlled archive access since the flood. POV: Sam. Emotional beat: courage outrunning caution.

chapters.title: Ruth's Ledger
chapters.summary: Confronted gently, Ruth breaks: she's been paid for thirty years to 'maintain' records by an anonymous account, never knowing what she was erasing. She surrenders the payment trail. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: complicity of small compromises.

chapters.title: Follow the Money
chapters.summary: The payments route through the Windrow Family Trust—meaning Cordelia, or her late mother, funded the cover-up. Quentin realizes the gala alibis were coordinated by the trust itself. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the web tightening around the top.

chapters.title: They Take Bo
chapters.summary: Bo is attacked and hospitalized after photographing the orchard well; the message is unmistakable. Quentin's rage finally has a face and a cost. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: fear transfigured into fury.

chapters.title: The Gala Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Working all night, the group rebuilds the 1994 gala timeline and finds the alibis share one flaw: a twenty-minute gap when the power failed, covered by a generator log signed by Augustus's son—the current judge. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the seam in the armor.

chapters.title: Judge Hale
chapters.summary: Judge Marcus Hale, Cordelia's husband and the founder's grandson, invites Quentin for a courteous conversation that is unmistakably a threat wrapped in civility. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: power smiling.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Choice
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts Cordelia privately; Cordelia reveals she discovered the fraud a decade ago and chose silence to protect her children's inheritance—then, shaken by Bo's attack, secretly hands Quentin her mother's letters. POV: Cordelia. Emotional beat: complicity cracking into conscience.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: The letters reveal Augustus himself staged his own empty coffin in 1961 to fake his death and flee debts; the family has been maintaining the myth ever since, killing to keep it buried. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: history as inheritance of sin.

chapters.title: No Safe House
chapters.summary: Quentin's apartment is searched; Anselm is pressured by the diocese to remove her from the archive. Her sanctuary is stripped away piece by piece. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: exile from the only home she had.

chapters.title: The Cathedral at Night
chapters.summary: Quentin sneaks in to retrieve the original grant and finds Judge Hale waiting—he confesses to arranging the three 'accidents' and Tomás's drowning, framing it as protecting the town itself. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: evil with a self-righteous face.

chapters.title: Run
chapters.summary: Quentin escapes with the document thanks to Sam's diversion and Dee's car; the group scatters to safe houses, deciding whether to go to Ibarra or take justice into their own hands. POV: Sam. Emotional beat: terror braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Ibarra's Hands Tied
chapters.summary: Ibarra confirms the warrant request was quashed from above—Hale controls the bench. Legal justice is a closed door. Quentin proposes another way. POV: Ibarra. Emotional beat: institutions failing, people stepping up.

chapters.title: The Plan
chapters.summary: The found family plans a public reckoning: the cathedral's Founder's Day service, where the whole town gathers beneath the empty crypt, becomes their stage. Each member takes a role. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: ordinary people choosing bravery.

chapters.title: Founder's Day
chapters.summary: During the service, Quentin presents the grant, the letters, and Ruth's ledger from the pulpit as Crane, brought to testify, names Hale before the congregation. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: truth spoken in a house of God.

chapters.title: The Fall of the Judge
chapters.summary: Hale attempts to flee through the crypt and is caught by Ibarra, who arrests him with witnesses everywhere; Cordelia publicly renounces the trust. POV: Ibarra. Emotional beat: justice arriving without violence.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Tomás Reyes is properly laid to rest, his name restored to the ledger in Quentin's hand; Marisol finally mourns. Anselm resigns, at peace. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief given its ceremony.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Quentin, reinstated and changed, adds her own name to the archive's contributors' page beside her mentor's—and stays for Sunday dinner at Dee's table, no longer invisible, no longer alone. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: home, claimed at last.
